updates.previous: SBA 7(a) minimum 10% equity injection required — up to half can be a seller note on full standby
updates.proposed: At least one lender now requires 15% full-cash equity injection for acquisitions over $500K, with no seller note credit toward the injection. Verify with each lender you contact — terms vary by institution. The 10/10/80 structure may not be available at all lenders for deals above $500K.
updates.reason: New lender guidance explicitly states 15% cash-only injection for acquisitions over $500K, with seller note excluded regardless of standby status.

updates.previous: Unlimited personal guarantee required for all owners with 20%+ stake
updates.proposed: Unlimited personal guarantee required for all owners with 20%+ stake. If your partner holds 20%+ and will not sign, they must be kept below 20% ownership — structure your entity accordingly before closing. This is a hard SBA requirement and cannot be waived.
updates.reason: User has disclosed that their partner will not sign a personal guarantee, which is a structural conflict requiring entity ownership to be arranged so the partner stays below 20%.

updates.previous: Minimum: $63,000 all-in on a $1M deal (5% cash injection + QoE + attorney at low end). Recommended: $100,000 all-in on a $1M deal (10% full cash injection + QoE + attorney at mid-range + contingency). Premium: $135,000+ if seller won't accept standby and you need full 10% cash plus advisor.
updates.proposed: Minimum: $63,000 all-in on a $1M deal if lender accepts 10/10/80 (confirm per lender). Recommended: $150,000+ all-in on a $1M deal if lender requires 15% cash-only injection ($150K injection + QoE + attorney). Premium: $175,000+ with advisor. Note: at least one lender now requires 15% cash-only for deals over $500K — model both scenarios until your specific lender confirms their requirement.
updates.reason: 15% cash-only injection at $1M deal = $150K, materially higher than the $50K–$100K previously modeled. User's $120K cash is below this threshold for a $1M deal.

updates.previous: Match to your liquid capital: minimum cash floor is 5% of purchase price if seller note is achievable, 10% if not.
updates.proposed: Match to your liquid capital with lender-specific injection requirement confirmed first. At $120K cash: (a) if lender accepts 10% cash injection, maximum deal size is ~$1.2M (10% of $1.2M = $120K, reserving nothing for fees — realistically ~$900K–$1M after fees); (b) if lender requires 15% cash-only injection, maximum deal size is ~$800K ($120K ÷ 15%) before fees — realistically $600K–$700K after professional fees. Confirm the injection requirement with your specific lender in Phase 1 before setting your deal size ceiling.
updates.reason: User disclosed $120K liquid capital. New lender guidance of 15% cash-only materially compresses the viable deal size range and must be reflected in the deal size decision.

updates.previous: What is your total liquid capital available for an equity injection, excluding retirement accounts?
updates.proposed: Liquid capital is confirmed at $120K. The critical open question is now: which lenders require 15% cash-only vs. 10% with seller note credit for acquisitions in your target size range? This determines whether your deal ceiling is ~$700K (15% lender) or ~$1M (10% lender). Ask each lender explicitly in your pre-qualification call.
updates.reason: User provided liquid capital figure. The blocking question shifts to lender-specific injection requirement, which now has material variability per the new lender guidance.

updates.previous: (no existing gotcha about partner guarantee or injection rate variability)
updates.proposed: Add two new gotchas: (1) Lender injection requirements now vary — at least one lender requires 15% cash-only for acquisitions over $500K with no seller note credit. Do not assume 10/10/80 is available at every lender. Ask the injection question in your first pre-qualification call. (2) A co-owner partner who will not sign a personal guarantee must be kept below 20% ownership in your acquisition entity. Structure this before you make any offers — SBA rules require every 20%+ owner to sign, and restructuring after LOI is signed creates lender problems.
updates.reason: New lender guidance on injection and user's disclosure about partner guarantee refusal are both material operational risks not covered in existing gotchas.

updates.previous: SBA 7(a) with seller note — 10% cash equity, 10% seller note on full standby, 80% SBA loan.
updates.proposed: SBA 7(a) — target structure depends on lender confirmed in Phase 1. Best case: 10% cash equity, 10% seller note on full standby, 80% SBA loan (10/10/80). If lender requires 15% cash-only injection (now confirmed at least one does for deals over $500K), structure becomes 15% cash, 85% SBA loan with no seller note toward injection. At $120K cash, this limits deal size to approximately $600K–$700K net of fees at a 15%-injection lender, or $900K–$1M at a 10%-injection lender. Confirm with each lender before setting deal size.
updates.reason: New lender guidance and user's $120K cash constraint combine to make the 10/10/80 structure lender-dependent rather than assumed.
